sceneFacts.shortVersion: Bradley Cooper was a chef before playing one.
sceneFacts.longDescription: Bradley Cooper was a chef before playing one. He worked as a busboy and prep cook at restaurants in New Jersey.

sceneFacts.shortVersion: Hear that music? It's from the Donnie Darko score.
sceneFacts.longDescription: Hear that music? It's from the Donnie Darko score. Several scenes in Burnt borrow Michael Andrews' cult classic cues.

sceneAnchor.anchorElement: Several scenes in Burnt incorporate cues from Michael Andrews' score for Donnie Darko, specifically "Cellar Door," "Carpathian Ridge," and "Gretchen Ross."

sceneFacts.shortVersion: Adam Jones was a mix of real-life celebrity chefs.
sceneFacts.longDescription: Adam Jones was a mix of real-life celebrity chefs. Bradley Cooper based the character on Gordon Ramsay, Marcus Wareing, and Marco Pierre White.

sceneAnchor.sceneDescription:
[scene 51] 00:16:59–00:17:17

cast on screen: Bradley Cooper
sceneAnchor.anchorElement: The fictional character Adam Jones was heavily influenced by real chefs like Gordon Ramsay, Marcus Wareing, Mario Batali, and Marco Pierre White.

sceneFacts.shortVersion: This kitchen set was a fully functioning, real kitchen.
sceneFacts.longDescription: This kitchen set was a fully functioning, real kitchen. Consultant chef Marcus Wareing ensured it worked as a real kitchen, even turning the stoves on full.

sceneFacts.shortVersion: Gordon Ramsay produced, and a Michelin chef created the food.
sceneFacts.longDescription: Gordon Ramsay produced, and a Michelin chef created the food. Consultant chef Marcus Wareing prepared all the recipes for the movie.

sceneFacts.shortVersion: The film's budget was reported as $20 million, but records show $32.7 million.
sceneFacts.longDescription: The film's budget was reported as $20 million, but records show $32.7 million. Louisiana film commission records indicated the higher figure.

sceneFacts.shortVersion: Burnt's distributor wanted a January release, but the board said no.
sceneFacts.longDescription: Burnt's distributor wanted a January release, but the board said no. The film was forced into an October slot to meet quarterly release quotas.

sceneFacts.shortVersion: Burnt had one of the worst opening weekends for a film in over 3,000 theaters.
sceneFacts.longDescription: Burnt had one of the worst opening weekends for a film in over 3,000 theaters. It pulled in just over $5 million, making it the 4th worst opening on record.

sceneFacts.shortVersion: Burnt was in development for 10 years, almost starring Keanu Reeves.
sceneFacts.longDescription: Burnt was in development for 10 years, almost starring Keanu Reeves. David Fincher was also slated to direct the film at one point.

sceneFacts.shortVersion: Burnt" filmed in New Orleans, London, and Ealing Studios.
sceneFacts.longDescription: Burnt" filmed in New Orleans, London, and Ealing Studios. The Langham Hotel in London was also a key filming location.

sceneFacts.shortVersion: The studio spent over $20M on ads for Burnt.
sceneFacts.longDescription: The studio spent over $20M on ads for Burnt. This included $12.3 million just for television commercials.
